To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the majority of childhood-onset asthma remits by middle age; (ii) childhood-onset asthma is more likely to remission than adult-onset; (iii) allergic rhinitis and eczema in childhood and later in life are negatively associated with asthma remission; (iv) maternal asthma and childhood chronic bronchiitis are negatively associated with remitting asthma; (v) passive smoking is negatively associated with asthma; (vi) adult smoking is positively associated with asthma

asthma remission in adulthood is more likely if the asthma started in childhood, if the asthma was not severe, if the asthma had not persisted for more than 2 years, and if there were fewer allergic comorbidities.
